highlights.title: On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Model Adaptation, an Effective Paradigm on Low-Quality Multimodal Data
highlights.summary: OnPoKD introduces the first on‑policy distillation framework for adapting vision‑language models, learning a lightweight controller that builds sample‑wise adaptive targets from reliability and disagreement cues.
highlights.detail: Previous methods used a fixed teacher‑prediction target, which can fail under class or domain shift. OnPoKD treats target construction as a dynamic policy decision, allowing per‑sample adaptation. The controller remains lightweight, enabling efficient training on low‑quality multimodal data. This approach aims to improve adaptation robustness without increasing model size.

highlights.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning
highlights.summary: A new framework combines a Geometric Vision Parser with a Symbolic Solver to let a pure LLM match state‑of‑the‑art multimodal models on challenging geometry problems from the 2025 Chinese Zhongkao exam.
highlights.detail: The system translates diagram images into symbolic representations, then applies formal logical deductions, reducing hallucinations common in large multimodal models. By using only an LLM plus specialized modules, it cuts computational cost while preserving interpretability. The benchmark ensures the evaluation covers novel, high‑school‑level geometry tasks.

highlights.title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
highlights.summary: Maverick proposes the first information‑theoretically sound protocol for privately delegating and verifiably computing matrix‑vector multiplications, the core operation in LLM inference.
highlights.detail: Existing privacy solutions either add heavy server overhead or rely on additional trust assumptions. Maverick’s protocol enables a client to offload the dominant matrix‑vector step to a third‑party while receiving a provable correctness guarantee. This reduces the computational burden on the client without sacrificing privacy or integrity, making private LLM inference more practical.

highlights.title: Breaking Fault Lines: Unifying TEE-Assisted BFT Consensus in Partially Trusted Worlds
highlights.summary: The paper derives a tight resilience bound f < max{n/3, m/2} for partially trusted TEE‑assisted BFT, showing TEEs boost fault tolerance only after covering > 2/3 of replicas.
highlights.detail: The authors introduce a dual‑quorum construction that safely mixes TEE‑only and mixed quorums. A fast‑path leader, protected by hardware non‑equivocation, reduces both consensus and view‑change latency. These concepts are realized in the Raftel protocol implementation, demonstrating practical performance gains.

highlights.title: GPT-6 Astra: The next generation in intelligence for work
highlights.summary: OpenAI announced GPT‑6 Astra, a business‑focused model offering enhanced reasoning, computer use, and improved writing and design judgment.
highlights.detail: GPT‑6 Astra is positioned as the most capable OpenAI model for enterprise workloads, extending the GPT‑6 series with stronger tool‑use abilities. It is expected to be integrated into OpenAI’s API offerings for tasks such as report generation, design critique, and automated decision support. The announcement highlights its suitability for professional environments.

items.title: Paul Christiano joins OpenAI Foundation Board
items.summary: Paul Christiano joined the OpenAI Foundation Board and its Safety and Security Committee, bringing AI alignment and safety expertise.
items.detail: Christiano is known for his work on AI alignment research and has previously collaborated with OpenAI on safety initiatives. His board membership may influence the foundation’s strategic direction on governance, risk assessment, and the development of safety standards for advanced AI systems.

items.title: The AI policy window is open. We need to act.
items.summary: Chris Lehane argues that the current policy window demands stronger AI safety evidence, shared standards, and durable policy action.
items.detail: Lehane emphasizes that rapid advances in AI capabilities create urgency for coordinated regulatory frameworks. He calls for transparent safety evaluations, industry‑wide standards, and long‑term policy measures before public concern wanes, positioning the window as a narrow opportunity for effective governance.

items.title: IBM releases SOTA Granite Time Series PatchTST-FM-r2 model with commercial-friendly license
items.summary: IBM released the Granite PatchTST‑FM‑r2 time‑series model, claimed SOTA and offered under a commercial‑friendly license.
items.detail: PatchTST‑FM‑r2 targets forecasting tasks and reportedly outperforms prior benchmarks on standard time‑series datasets. The commercial‑friendly license permits integration into proprietary products without restrictive clauses, aiming to broaden adoption in industry applications such as demand planning and anomaly detection.

items.title: Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
items.summary: DeepSeek‑V4.1‑Flash, an image‑text‑to‑text model on Hugging Face, has received 365 likes.
items.detail: The model extends the DeepSeek series with capabilities to generate textual descriptions from images and vice versa. Community interest, reflected by the 365 likes, suggests relevance for multimodal applications such as captioning, visual question answering, and content creation.

items.title: Security updates for Wednesday
items.summary: Wednesday security updates were issued for multiple Linux distributions, covering packages such as expat, glib2, redis, kernel, and others.
items.detail: The updates span AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Red Hat, SUSE, and Ubuntu, addressing vulnerabilities in core libraries, networking tools, and system services. Administrators are advised to apply the patches promptly to mitigate potential exploits across the affected environments.

items.title: A decade of Rustls
items.summary: Rustls celebrated ten years since its first commit on May 2 2016, with its 0.23 release launched on Feb 29 2024 after 43 non‑breaking updates.
items.detail: The project achieved early web interoperability within a month of its initial commit, and the 0.23 line introduced features like FIPS support while maintaining API stability. Over eight years, Rustls evolved through numerous releases, positioning itself as a mature, security‑focused TLS library aiming for a 1.0 milestone.

items.title: LibreOffice Base survey results
items.summary: A survey of 455 LibreOffice Base users, including over 330 Linux users, highlighted demand for a cleaner UI, better search, stability, and performance improvements.
items.detail: Respondents cited cluttered interfaces and limited search functionality as primary pain points, while also requesting bug fixes and faster query processing. The feedback will inform upcoming development priorities for Base, especially regarding cross‑platform consistency and enterprise‑grade reliability.

items.title: [$] LWN.net Weekly Edition for September 10, 2026
items.summary: The LWN weekly edition for September 10 2026 covers Rust’s never type, Debian and CERN news, memory tiering, multithreaded Python testing, TCMalloc fixes, and briefs on Rustls, Asahi Linux, Buildroot 2026.08, and more.
items.detail: The issue features in‑depth articles on emerging language features and performance engineering, alongside concise briefs on recent releases such as Audacity 4.0 and Jellyfin 12.0. It serves as a snapshot of current open‑source developments and upcoming conference announcements.

items.title: [$] Typst makes big strides
items.summary: Typst 0.15, released June, adds variable fonts, MathML, multiple bibliographies, and more, and remains free under Apache‑2.0, written in Rust.
items.detail: The update also introduces support for variable font axes, enabling dynamic typographic variation. MathML output allows direct embedding of mathematical markup for web use. Multiple bibliography files can be managed simultaneously, simplifying large technical documents. All components are implemented in safe Rust, preserving the project's performance and security goals.

items.title: 3D Printable Lenticular Indicators
items.summary: Hackaday showcases 3D‑printable lenticular indicators for visual feedback.
items.detail: Lenticular indicators use layered micro‑structures to create depth or motion effects that change with viewing angle. By 3D printing these structures, creators can embed status displays directly onto prototypes or devices. The approach is useful for low‑cost, on‑device diagnostics without electronics.

items.title: Introducing Consort: A Spec-First Agent Framework for Enforced, Test-Driven Development on Live Database Branches
items.summary: Consort is a spec‑first agent framework that enforces test‑driven development on live database branches.
items.detail: Consort distinguishes three enforcement modes: persuasion (soft prompts), front‑loaded structure (strong specs with trusted builds), and immutable controls (deterministic orchestrators, human‑approved gates, and immutable test results). It integrates with existing CI pipelines to keep agent‑generated code reliable.

items.title: Violet: Enabling Full Virtualization for M-mode RTOS on RISC-V
items.summary: Violet hypervisor adds full virtualization support for M‑mode, allowing RTOSes like FreeRTOS or Zephyr to run in virtual machines on RISC‑V.
items.detail: Prior RISC‑V virtualization only covered U‑mode and S‑mode, leaving M‑mode RTOSes unvirtualized. Violet extends the privilege hierarchy, enabling isolation of real‑time workloads similar to ARM and x86 hypervisors. This opens possibilities for mixed‑criticality systems on a single RISC‑V platform.

items.title: Stencil Computation at the Intersection of AI and HPC
items.summary: Using Tensor compilers, an 8th‑order 25‑point acoustic stencil runs at 15.6 Gpts/s on Battlemage B580 with TinyTC, beating the PyTorch/Triton implementation’s 13.5 Gpts/s, and reaches 35.8 Gpts/s on zero‑initialized data.
items.detail: The study also evaluated Intel B70, GPU MAX 1550, NVIDIA A100/RTX6000 Blackwell/H100, and AMD MI325x, confirming consistent gains on hardware with memory compression. Roofline analysis shows the TinyTC version better utilizes compute‑bound regions, while the PyTorch version remains more portable across devices.

items.title: UnsafeChecker: Finding Soundness Bugs in Rust Safe Abstractions
items.summary: UnsafeChecker is a compiler‑integrated static analysis framework that detects potential soundness violations in Rust safe abstractions built on unsafe code.
items.detail: Existing C/C++ analyzers ignore Rust's ownership model, and current Rust tools lack deep semantic tracking of raw‑pointer contexts. UnsafeChecker instruments the compiler to model lifetimes and pointer provenance, flagging unsafe blocks that could break safety guarantees before code reaches production.

items.title: Decentralized network congestion control for DAG-based distributed ledger system
items.summary: The paper proposes a node‑specific, behavior‑based proof‑of‑work model to mitigate congestion in DAG‑based distributed ledger networks.
items.detail: Transaction spamming, rapid user growth, and token launches often overload DAG ledgers. By adjusting PoW difficulty per node based on recent behavior, the scheme throttles abusive actors while preserving throughput for honest participants. The authors evaluate impact on transactions‑per‑second and consensus latency.

items.title: Tencent/teamai-cli
items.summary: teamai-cli is a command‑line tool from Tencent that streamlines making every team AI‑native.
items.detail: The CLI wraps common AI workflows—model selection, dataset handling, and inference serving—into simple commands, enabling non‑specialist teams to integrate large‑language models and embeddings into their products without writing custom glue code.

items.title: 7h30th3r0n3/Evil-M5Project
items.summary: Evil‑M5Project is a C++ tool for ethical Wi‑Fi hacking, supporting Cardputer, Atoms3, Fire, and core2 platforms.
items.detail: It provides scanning, monitoring, and interaction capabilities for Wi‑Fi networks in a controlled lab environment. Designed for education, the project demonstrates protocol vulnerabilities and packet injection techniques while enforcing responsible use policies.

items.title: OpenDCAI/GameFactory-3A
items.summary: GameFactory‑3A is an open‑source Python framework for generating AAA‑level game assets and mechanics.
items.detail: The framework bundles procedural content generation, AI‑driven asset creation, and physics simulation modules, allowing developers to prototype full‑featured game experiences with minimal manual art pipelines.

items.title: anbeime/skill
items.summary: skill is a Python repository that aggregates the most up‑to‑date AI agent skill packs across domains, auto‑curating thousands of GitHub projects.
items.detail: It periodically scrapes GitHub for skill repositories, ranks them by stars and recent activity, and packages them for one‑click installation. The collection spans document processing, content creation, programming assistance, machine‑learning pipelines, and workflow automation.

items.title: pascalorg/editor
items.summary: pascalorg/editor is an open-source 3D architectural editor that includes a local command‑line interface, MCP tools, and workflows designed for both human users and AI agents.
items.detail: The tool targets architectural modeling with scripts run via its CLI and provides multi‑component processing utilities to automate repetitive tasks. Its open‑source license encourages community contributions and integration into AI‑driven pipelines.

items.title: NVIDIA/nccl
items.summary: NVIDIA/nccl provides optimized primitives for collective multi‑GPU communication in C++.
items.detail: NCCL implements bandwidth‑optimal algorithms for operations such as all‑reduce, broadcast, and reduce‑scatter, enabling large‑scale deep‑learning training. It is integrated into major frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow and is maintained as an open‑source project on GitHub.
